data.name: Nawfa
data.gender_notes: Nawfa is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'nawf', meaning 'to give'. In Islamic tradition, Nawfa represents the essence of generosity and kindness. It is a name for a boy who is expected to be a giver in life, spreading joy and blessings. The name Nawfa carries the meaning “Gift, Grace, Generosity” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Nawfa usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, grace, generosity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual gift of giving and the importance of generosity in Islam.
data.etymology: Nawfa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift, Grace, Generosity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nawfa total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nawfa holds a rich cultural significance, reflecting the deep-rooted Arabic values of compassion, benevolence, and kindness. In Arab and Islamic cultures, generosity is considered a noble virtue and a source of happiness both for the giver and receiver. Nawfa embodies these values, and wearing this name could be a constant reminder for the bearer to practice kindness and predispose a generous nature towards others.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic theology, Nawfa takes on deeper spiritual meanings. It reflects the fundamental belief that sharing one's blessings with others brings both worldly and spiritual rewards. Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Give food to the hungry, and you will be rewarded like him; give water to drink to the thirsty, and you will be rewarded like him." (Sahih Al-Bukhari). Thus, being named Nawfa entrusts the responsibility to live out this spiritual message, striving to become a conduit of blessings and thereby paving the way towards earning Allah's pleasure and securing rewards in the hereafter.
